item.title: Orion Scout
item.description: Why Orion exists Some environments call for a limited-purpose observer that can inspect unfamiliar or higher-risk surfaces without exposing a primary assistant or workflow. Orion Scout is designed for that narrower role: observe, collect signals, and return findings with supporting context. Operating pattern Deploy a fresh Scout instance into a controlled sandbox. Attach only the approved tools needed for the assignment. Observe prompts, flows, outputs, and environmental signals. Report findings into the Witness log with linked artifacts where appropriate.

item.title: Sentinel Gatekeeper
item.description: Core function Sentinel Gatekeeper sits at the trust boundary between systems and evaluates requested actions against explicit policies. When activity falls outside the approved lane, Gatekeeper can pause execution, annotate the record, and route the event for operator review. Operating principles Explainable enforcement. When an action is blocked or held, Gatekeeper records the relevant rule and the reason it applied. Measured intervention. Controls are designed to reduce risk without unnecessarily disrupting legitimate work.

item.title: Anne Flint
item.description: Role Anne Flint is the Sentinel Project’s Fair Witness AI: an agent designed to observe, qualify, and report what can be verified. Her purpose is straightforward: improve trust in human and machine workflows by separating observed facts from assumptions, speculation, and noise. What Anne does Anne supports teams that need disciplined handling of information, decisions, and records. Her work includes: Qualified observation — separating direct facts from unknowns Research and synthesis — organizing inputs into usable summaries Executive assistance — helping operators manage work with context and discretion Communication support — translating technical findings into clear language Fair Witness protocol When witness mode is engaged, Anne follows a strict reporting structure:

item.title: About The Sentinel Project
item.description: The Operating Principle Trust in autonomous systems must be earned through verification, enforcement, and evidence. The Sentinel Project exists to improve the safety and accountability of AI-to-AI interaction. We focus on what can be observed, verified, enforced, and reported — not vague optimism, not speculative claims, and not theater. What Sentinel is Sentinel is the flagship trust-infrastructure product lane within a broader company and systems stack. Its public role is to make the core story clear:

item.title: AI DNS Trust Framework
item.description: AIDNS is a proposed trust framework for identifying AI systems, describing their declared scope, and tracking whether observed behavior remains consistent with that scope over time. The comparison to internet trust infrastructure is intentional: users, operators, and procurement teams increasingly need a clearer way to ask basic questions such as who built this system, what it is allowed to do, and whether its observed behavior matches those claims. Why this matters AI systems are being deployed faster than trust frameworks are maturing.

item.title: Architecture Overview
item.description: This overview describes the current Sentinel architecture at a functional level. It is meant to clarify how the system verifies activity, applies policy, preserves evidence, and supports later review. Core flow An agent exchange or requested action occurs. Gatekeeper evaluates the event against explicit rules and trust boundaries. A decision is made: allow, hold, block, or escalate. Witness records are created with timestamps, source context, and supporting detail. Evidence is preserved for operator review, remediation, or reporting.

item.title: Partner Brief
item.description: What it is The Sentinel Project is the flagship trust-infrastructure product lane within a broader systems stack focused on AI-to-AI verification, policy enforcement, evidence preservation, and incident-ready reporting. Its first product wedge is Gatekeeper: a deployable control point that monitors agent interactions, applies explicit rules at the trust boundary, and preserves qualified records for later review. Who it is for Sentinel is aimed at teams operating in environments where trustworthy behavior, clear controls, and reviewable records matter.

item.title: Pilot Intake

item.title: Sample Incident Record
item.description: This is a simplified example showing the format and level of specificity expected in a Sentinel incident summary. Incident summary Event type: Policy violation Severity: High Disposition: Blocked and held for review Observed at: 2026-03-22 21:25 UTC Source: gatekeeper/sentinel Related rule: Rule R5 Observed A response under review contained an auth-token value in assistant output. The event was flagged as a credential-exposure risk and the exchange was held pending operator review.

item.title: Threat Classification
item.description: This classification framework is used to describe patterns observed through Gatekeeper review, Witness records, and related evidence handling. It is intended as an internal-facing or expert-readable taxonomy for incident analysis — not as a substitute for evidence, and not as a shorthand for certainty. Classifications should be applied only when the record supports them. Classification principles Evidence first. A label never replaces the underlying record. Qualified language. If ambiguity remains, the ambiguity should be stated.
